title: Definition and First Rule
teaches: A 'Glint number' is a whole number whose last digit is not zero and which is divisible by that last digit. Specifically, any number ending in 1 is always a Glint number.
visual: The number 21 appears center-screen. The digit '1' pulses green while the rest of the number fades slightly. Text below reads: 'Glint Number: Last digit ≠ 0 AND Number ÷ Last Digit = Whole'. A checkmark animates next to 21.
narration: We define a Glint number as a whole number ending in a non-zero digit that divides itself evenly. For instance, every number ending in 1 is automatically a Glint number because any integer divided by 1 results in a whole number.

title: The Zero Exclusion Rule
teaches: Rule 2: A number ending in 0 is never a Glint number.
visual: The number 50 appears. The digit '0' turns red and shakes horizontally. A large red 'X' stamps over the screen. Text below reads: 'Rule: Ending in 0 is NEVER Glint'.
narration: However, there is a strict exclusion rule: any number ending in zero can never be a Glint number. This is because division by zero is undefined, preventing the divisibility condition from being met.

title: The Five Inclusion Rule
teaches: Rule 3: A number ending in 5 is always a Glint number.
visual: The number 75 appears. The digit '5' pulses gold. An equation animates below: '75 ÷ 5 = 15'. A green checkmark appears next to the result. Text reads: 'Rule: Ending in 5 is ALWAYS Glint'.
narration: Similarly, any number ending in five is always a Glint number. Since all integers ending in 5 are divisible by 5 with no remainder, they satisfy our definition perfectly.
